clue.text: Countersign with something less effective than father's pen

annotationWithheld.why: Countersign with something less effective than father's pen (8): PA'S + SWORD, but SWORD is read from 'something less effective than [father's] pen', so 'father's' does two jobs (PA'S and part of the proverb phrase); no single-job parse exists
annotationWithheld.clue: Countersign with something less effective than father's pen

clue.text: A married woman in the country

parts.note: Erica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife living abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: America is the common name for the United States.

clue.text: Room on vessel required for visiting stars

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: space is room
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: Accommodation on a ship is needed to visit celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft for interstellar travel is what one would need to reach other suns.

clue.text: Captain having novel connection with the sea

explanation.surface: A ship's master with a fictional link to the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The skipper is slangily called the old man; Hemingway's novel is The Old Man and the Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew slang for the skipper, and Hemingway's novella pairs this figure with the ocean.

parts.note: the phrase for blatant overcharging, read literally, is a theft committed in broad light

explanation.surface: Excessive prices of this kind are obviously criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a blatant rip-off, taken literally, is a theft committed openly in the sunlit hours.

explanation.surface: A small share goes to the runner trailing the podium finishers.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter is one of four equal parts, and the finisher after gold, silver and bronze comes next in line.

clue.text: Sort of boot needed in season

definitions.text: Sort of boot needed in season

parts.words: Sort of boot needed in season
parts.note: a kind of studded boot worn during the winter sporting season, and to boot is also to kick

explanation.surface: A particular kind of footwear is required at certain times of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Studded boots are worn for the winter sport played over a season.

clue.text: Smuggle a sort of whisky or port

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running
corn whiskey is an American spirit made from maize

explanation.surface: Bring in contraband whisky or fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink to go with whisky, but it is a town: Runcorn is a port on the Mersey in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Runcorn is a docks town in Cheshire, a harbour on the Manchester Ship Canal.

explanation.surface: Industrial action taken by agricultural labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: A haymaker is also a wild, swinging punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands who cut and dry grass on a farm, and heavy swinging punches.

explanation.surface: Think about something from one particular angle.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem or think about something is one sense; 'in some regard' means in some respect or aspect.

clue.text: Volunteers in the old army, on being organized

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of 'the', as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

indicators.note: being put in order signals that the letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Volunteers serving in the army of the past, once it had been properly arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being organized' rearranges YE (old 'the'), ARMY and ON together.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeomanry were British volunteer cavalry forces raised from landowning farmers.

clue.text: Scholars at one with first volume of Americans

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of the metric volume litre
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Academics, together with the opening tome of a study of Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with first' tells you the American volume goes at the front, before AT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the educated, literary class of people.

clue.text: To travel between A and B, returns to capital

indicators.note: returns means the whole assembled string is read backwards
between means the travel words sit inside the A and B

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Someone shuttles between two points and goes back to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A and B' are just the letters, not points on a map; 'between' places the travel words inside them, and 'returns' reads the whole result backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the capital city of Colombia.

parts.note: a pash is an informal word for a crush or infatuation

explanation.surface: Someone develops a crush on a provincial ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman official who governed a province.

parts.note: Pará is a state of Brazil, also known for Para rubber and Para nuts
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A horse from Brazil is the best of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means of chief importance, above all others.

explanation.surface: Someone insists on number one in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The '1' refers to 1 across: a sentry's call demands the countersign before anyone may pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry's call of 'Who goes there?' is a demand for the countersign; to question or contest something is the other sense.

parts.note: the person with the last word on a newspaper's content states the paper's view in a leading article

explanation.surface: Someone with the casting vote voices a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article in a newspaper sets out the paper's own view.

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means they are reordered into a new form

explanation.surface: An orchard owner offers a range of witty comebacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear tree bears the fruit, so it is literally the grower of that fruit.

explanation.surface: A schoolboy who was beaten blows a derisive noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Raspberries grow on canes; a rude noise made with the tongue and lips is also called a raspberry.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit grows on woody stems called canes, and blowing one is a mocking sound made with the lips.

parts.note: in the Seven Ages of Man speech from As You Like It, the fourth and middle age is the fighting man

explanation.surface: A man in his forties from one of Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaques's speech lists seven ages, and the fourth, central one is the warrior seeking reputation.

explanation.surface: Textbooks bought for university study.
explanation.walkthrough: King's College is in Cambridge (and London); 1 and 2 Kings are books of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: King's is a famous Cambridge college, and First and Second Kings are Old Testament books.

clue.text: With bad grace, I provide direction for classicist

indicators.note: bad signals that grace and I are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Grudgingly, I give instructions for a scholar of antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges GRACE and I into GRECIA, then N is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A Grecian is a scholar of Greek language and literature.

clue.text: Misused characters change sides in time

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an era is a period of time
to rat is to desert or defect to the other side

explanation.surface: Wrongly used letters swap places over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change sides' looks like part of the surface's swapped letters, but to rat is to defect; 'in' places it inside the period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are printing mistakes, letters set wrongly in type.

parts.note: not an author from the tropics but the American writer of Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn

explanation.surface: A writer from a hot climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Miller wrote the novels Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn.

explanation.surface: A sportsman keeps raising money for someone in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf the borrow is the allowance for slope on a green: a putter borrows by deliberately aiming up the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer allowing for slope aims above the hole, and a person who takes a loan owes money.

clue.text: Everything I have hidden by devious nurse

indicators.note: hidden by means the I have letters are tucked inside the other piece
devious, meaning winding or crooked, signals the word nurse is rearranged

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A scheming nurse conceals all I own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges the nurse's letters, and 'hidden by' tucks the contraction of 'I have' inside them, after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the whole of existence, all that there is.

clue.text: Excuses made by almost all the birds

indicators.note: almost means the word all is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: ibis is a wading bird, and the word is the same in the plural

explanation.surface: Explanations offered by nearly every one of the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Alibis are pleas that one was elsewhere, used loosely for any justifications.

clue.text: Most of the people in ancient state

indicators.note: most of means not quite all the letters of the people phrase are used, one being dropped

parts.note: the race is the people, a nation or ethnic group

explanation.surface: A majority of the population lived in an old country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops an E from THE RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region and kingdom in the south-east Balkans.

explanation.surface: A question about a horse, answered with 'more than one'.
explanation.walkthrough: A yearling is in its second year, so it is past the age of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A young racehorse aged between one and two years; its age exceeds a single year.
